clue.text: A woman can expect some improvement in the personal service here

definitions.text: A woman can expect some improvement in the personal service here

parts.words: A woman can expect some improvement in the personal service here
parts.note: the personal service is hair, nails and make-up, and the improvement is to her looks: the clue describes a salon visit

explanation.surface: A customer is promised better attention from staff somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon offering hairdressing and cosmetic treatments is where clients go to have their appearance improved.

clue.text: Send tea for distribution around Docklands

indicators.note: letters handed out for distribution are scattered, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone orders tea to be delivered around London's old dock district.
explanation.walkthrough: The EAST END is the traditionally working-class part of London that surrounds the redeveloped Docklands.
explanation.definitionFit: The district of east London lies around the former docks, now called Docklands.

clue.text: Employed in a private house doing the cleaning

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow, across the join of two words

explanation.surface: Someone worked as a domestic, cleaning a private home.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is hoUSE Doing; the rest of the clue dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Employed and used both mean put to work or made use of.

clue.text: Americans ask for no backing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the whole string of both words is read from the end

parts.note: to ask for something is to seek it
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Americans make a request and are refused support.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is an informal name for people from the United States.

clue.text: He'll support a superior

parts.note: better means superior

explanation.surface: A man promises to back someone above him.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor or abetter is one who encourages or assists another, often in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Grassland parking will be available in spring

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A meadow will offer space for cars in the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is the verb or noun for a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a jump or bound.

clue.text: How a continental twit's made to unwind

parts.note: un is French for a, a word from the Continent

indicators.note: made here means made into something else, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A foolish European is persuaded to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals the anagram of TWITS (twit's without the apostrophe) to TWIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwist is to undo the coils of something, to wind it back loose.

clue.text: People getting down to work in the main

definitions.text: People getting down to work in the main

parts.words: People getting down to work in the main
parts.note: read the main as the ocean and getting down as descending, not as starting work generally

explanation.surface: Most people are knuckling under to their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers descend into the ocean depths for their work; the main is poetic for the sea.

clue.text: Rent ducal seal for use in the dukes place

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman's seal is hired out for use at a duke's home.
explanation.walkthrough: ARUNDEL CASTLE in West Sussex, England, is the seat of the Dukes of Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sussex fortress is the family seat of the Duke of Norfolk.

clue.text: Oriental models are sent

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: Fashion models from Asia have been dispatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like a noun for people but is a verb, telling us to reshape ARE SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from the East.

clue.text: The man pressing a claim as a former player

parts.note: ex means former
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A man demands his due as a retired performer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who demands or insists on payment or a right.

clue.text: Look both ways

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards, so it looks both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An instruction to check left and right, as before crossing a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a quick look or glance.

clue.text: A Greek character's all mouth!

definitions.meaning: the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet
a river's broad mouth where it spreads into many channels

explanation.surface: Someone from Greece is all talk.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the Greek letter D and the fan-shaped mouth of a river such as the Nile.

clue.text: A living dog is better than a dead "Ecclesiastes

definitions.text: A living dog is better than a dead "Ecclesiastes

parts.words: A living dog is better than a dead "Ecclesiastes
parts.note: complete the Bible verse from Ecclesiastes 9:4 with the missing final word

explanation.surface: A Bible proverb holds that being alive matters more than strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The verse contrasts a humble live dog with the dead king of beasts.

clue.text: A large piece of the Western border

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for western
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A big slice of land on the western frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a thick chunk, as of cheese or cake.

clue.text: Article about a woman, not in the least colourful

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
she is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a lady describes her as dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale or grey, drained of colour.

clue.text: Not reaching any conclusion

parts.note: read literally as having no finish rather than failing to decide

explanation.surface: A debate that never settles anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Something interminable has no finish, so it goes on for ever.

clue.text: Favour getting trees to set out

indicators.note: to set out is to arrange or lay out, so the letters are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A gardener is granted permission to plant trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' is the noun for a ribbon badge worn to show support, not a kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a knot of ribbon worn as a badge, as at a wedding or show.

clue.text: Plans of the French receiving Mark!

indicators.note: receiving means taking another piece in, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: des is French for of the (plural)
a sign is a mark

explanation.surface: French plans are being marked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs and plans are both schemes drawn up beforehand.

clue.text: Interview an attendant when there's some leak

parts.note: to see someone can mean to interview them
a page is a boy attendant

explanation.surface: Questioning a servant about some leaked information.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid escaping slowly, a gradual leakage.

clue.text: A tough guy to fight and beat

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do
to tan is to beat, as in tan someone's hide

explanation.surface: A hard man is ready to brawl and win.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan is someone hardy and austere, like the citizens of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: He's wary where giving credit is concerned

definitions.text: He's wary where giving credit is concerned

parts.words: He's wary where giving credit is concerned
parts.note: credit means belief, not money lent: a cautious lender is the false picture

explanation.surface: A cautious banker hesitates to lend money.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter is reluctant to believe what he is told.

clue.text: Making great efforts to get pound in discount

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a saving is a discount
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Working hard to get money off.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaving means toiling very hard, working like a slave.

clue.text: A person travelling to an old city and its ruins

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: something in ruins is broken up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A traveller heads for an ancient city and its remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone travelling for pleasure.

clue.text: Struggle with Welsh capital survey

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: a capital letter here is the initial, the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A contest between two Welsh cities over surveys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh capital' suggests Cardiff, but it is just the first letter of Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey something is to look at it, to take a view of it.

clue.text: To exclude a trainee is commonplace

parts.note: to ban is to exclude
L is the learner plate on a trainee driver's car

explanation.surface: Banning an apprentice is an ordinary event.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite, ordinary and unoriginal.

clue.text: The cat would upset saints

annotationWithheld.why: The cat would upset saints (4): SS from saints leaves PU with no clue word to give UP reversed, unless upset is split as UP + SET, which the grammar cannot take from one word.

clue.text: A fellow in distress has to turn in

annotationWithheld.why: A fellow in distress has to turn in (4): turn gives WIND but no parse found for the rest (a fellow, distress); the OCR clue may be garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: A fellow in distress has to turn in

clue.text: Enjoy a match

definitions.meaning: an equal, as in we shall not see his equal

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fond of is the verb sense; an equal counterpart is the noun sense.

clue.text: The individual accepting the truth about a certain leaning

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a list is a lean, as of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone facing facts about a particular bias.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatist faces facts as they are rather than as he would like them.

clue.text: Original one — one in Latin maybe

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
maybe suggests a possible version, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An original Roman item, perhaps one written in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns LATIN into NTIAL, and 'in' puts the second I inside it to give NITIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first or at the beginning, the original stage.

clue.text: They attend to witness the constitution of union

definitions.text: They attend to witness the constitution of union

parts.words: They attend to witness the constitution of union
parts.note: the union is a marriage and its constitution is the ceremony that forms it, not a political charter

explanation.surface: Delegates gather to observe the founding of a political union.
explanation.definitionFit: Invited guests come to see a couple joined in marriage.
